course_name_original: Gestión de Tecnologías de la Información
prerequisites: It is recommended to have successfully completed the course 'Configuración y Evaluación de Sistemas' from 3rd year and to be currently taking 'Ingeniería de Servicios' from the first semester of 4th year.
Ability to read and understand documentation written in English.

learning_outcomes.text: Ability to understand the environment of an organization and its needs in the field of information and communication technologies.

Ability to use user- and organization-centered methodologies for the development of applications and systems based on information technologies that ensure the accessibility, ergonomics, and usability of the systems.

Ability to use user- and organization-centered methodologies for the evaluation of applications and systems based on information technologies that ensure the accessibility, ergonomics, and usability of the systems.

Ability to use user- and organization-centered methodologies for the management of applications and systems based on information technologies that ensure the accessibility, ergonomics, and usability of the systems.
Know the methodologies and good practice guides used for information technology management.
Manage the design of IT services and their capacity and continuity levels.
Manage the transition of IT services, their configuration and deployment.
Evaluate the portfolio of IT services and their impact on business strategy.
Manage the operation of IT services with their incidents, problems, and events.
Manage the continuous improvement process of IT services.

syllabus_topics: Introduction to Service Management and ITIL v3
ITSM process simulation with the Apollo 13 case study

assessment_methods.method: Team simulation (ITSM processes with Apollo 13 case study)
Team work (complete management of an IT service)

assessment_rules: For the ordinary call, evaluation is continuous and consists of four parts: Theory (two partial controls, average of scores), Class Participation (gamified questionnaires), Team Simulation (ITSM process with Apollo 13 case study, public defense required), and Team Work (complete IT service management, memory and public defense required, 80% attendance to lab sessions required). To pass, Theory, Team Simulation, and Team Work must score at least 5 out of 10. The final grade is calculated as: 0.30 * Theory + 0.15 * Class Participation + 0.15 * Team Simulation + 0.4 * Team Work. If minimum scores are not met, the final grade is the minimum of the calculated grade and 4.5. For extraordinary calls, it consists of a final global theory exam (60%) and the team work (40%) from the ordinary call, which is carried over. Both parts must score at least 5 out of 10. For differentiated evaluation, it consists of a final global theory exam (60%) and an individual work (40%). In the ordinary call, partial theory controls can substitute the final theory exam; in extraordinary calls, ordinary call scores are retained. Both parts must score at least 5 out of 10.
